hero.heading:
Hindu content API
for developers.
hero.lede: One REST API for Sanskrit mantras, scripture books and chapters, linked recordings, and astrology calculations.

story.quote: Mantrilo powers the parts of Satyam our users turn to for daily practice. It helps them read and listen to Sanskrit mantras, explore the Bhagavad Gita chapter by chapter, check their local Panchang, and generate their Vedic birth chart. It’s been a great partner in bringing all of that into one app.

about.title: About Mantrilo.
about.lede: One developer API for Sanskrit content and astrology calculations.
about.serves: Mantrilo helps developers build Hindu devotional, learning and calendar apps. The API organizes mantra verses, scripture collections and available recordings, and calculates astrology data from inputs your app supplies.
about.catalog: Original text, transliteration, translation and audio are separate fields. Coverage varies by record. Preserve source references where supplied, and verify the edition, translator or performer with Mantrilo before using a title commercially.
about.sandbox: The sandbox uses a limited sample. Check the <library>Library</library> and <docs>API docs</docs> to see data formats, then <contact>contact Mantrilo</contact> for title-specific rights and coverage.

license.title: Content license status.
license.lede: Reuse guidance for Sanskrit texts, modern editions, and English retellings.
license.public: You can reuse original Sanskrit text in a commercial app where the text is in the public domain. Check the specific edition and the countries where you plan to distribute it. Keep the source reference with the text where available.
license.modern: Modern translations, commentary, editorial additions, and prose retellings can have separate rights. This includes the English retellings of the Ramayana and Mahabharata in the Books API. Check the terms for the version you plan to use and follow its attribution requirements.
license.questions: For reuse questions or rights concerns, <link>contact Mantrilo</link> with the title or source reference and a brief description of how you plan to use the material.

privacy.title: Privacy & data.
privacy.lede: What this website does with the details you enter.
privacy.warning: A final operator privacy policy has not been supplied. Review and provide it before launch.
privacy.preview: The contact form prepares a draft locally in your browser. It does not submit form entries to a server or save them in browser storage. If you download a draft, the file contains the details you entered. If configured, the email link passes the draft to your chosen email app.
privacy.referral: The public site keeps a broad referral category for the current tab. When you choose to try the API or open signup, the link includes that category and the public page path so Mantrilo can count Console visits and signup starts. It does not include the referring URL, account details, or request inputs. The developer console handles account registration and billing separately.

terms.warning: Final website terms have not been supplied. This status page is not a service agreement.

terms.keys: API keys are issued in the developer console. Preparing a message on the contact page does not create an account or start a subscription.
terms.commercial: Commercial integration is subject to the documented content license. The final service terms and content license must be provided and reviewed before onboarding customers.

search-mantras.name: Build a searchable mantra library
search-mantras.summary: List mantras and shlokas, filter by deity, and search the titles you have loaded.
search-mantras.render: Display data[].title, deity.name and verseCount. Use nextCursor for the next page. Open a row by passing its id to GET /v1/mantras/{id}.
search-mantras.inputs: Use limit (1–100, default 20), cursor (the previous nextCursor), and optional deity (a deity ID such as annapurna). The Mantras route also serves shlokas. The API has no full-text search parameter. The example filters one loaded page by title and optionally by audio availability. For catalog-wide search, index permitted content in your backend.
search-mantras.usage: Each successful page, deity-filter request, and detail fetch uses one request. Searching or filtering audio on already loaded results, or serving an entire response from your own cache without calling Mantrilo, uses zero Mantrilo requests.

featured-mantra.name: Add a daily mantra or featured shloka
featured-mantra.summary: Fetch a selected mantra and present its original Sanskrit and transliteration.
featured-mantra.render: Render data.title and the verses array. Display sanskrit and transliteration when present. The translation field is currently null.
featured-mantra.inputs: Use the stable id from the catalog. Choose or schedule the featured ID in your app. The API supplies the selected entry.
featured-mantra.usage: Each successful detail fetch uses one request. Reusing an entry already in your backend cache uses no additional request.

sacred-audio.name: Play a sacred recording
sacred-audio.summary: Request a temporary playback URL for an entry with a recording.
sacred-audio.render: Pass data.url to your player, and request a fresh link after data.expiresAt. The example response substitutes a placeholder for the expired signed URL.
sacred-audio.inputs: Use audio.href from the mantra record and append ?format=json. If audio is null, hide the player. The plain endpoint redirects to the recording. JSON mode gives your backend the signed URL.
sacred-audio.usage: Each successful link issuance uses one request and charges the full file size in bytes against audio allowance. Reading the already issued URL in the player makes no new Mantrilo API request.

upanishads.name: Load the Upanishads into your app
upanishads.summary: Call one collection directly, page through it, then open a book, chapter or verse.
upanishads.render: List data[].title and description, then open a book with GET /v1/books/{id}. Its chapters[] gives the chapter numbers for GET /v1/books/{id}/chapters/{chapter}, whose verses[] carry each verse number.
upanishads.inputs: collection is a collection id: upanishads, bhagavad-gita, advaita-vedanta-prakarana-granthas, vedanta or yoga. limit is 1–100 (default 24). Pass nextCursor as cursor for the next page; it is null on the last page. Every book in the response carries collection.id, so the same id works for links back to the collection. Sandbox keys return Isha Upanishad for this collection, with nextCursor set to null. Paid keys can page through the available collection. Collections without a designated sample return an empty sandbox page.
upanishads.usage: Each collection page, book index and chapter page uses one request. Paging three books at a time through a collection of twelve uses four requests.

book-reader.name: Build a book reader
book-reader.summary: Read Sanskrit verses or English retellings of the Ramayana and Mahabharata.
book-reader.render: Use the book title and chapter index for navigation. Scripture chapters return verses for available Sanskrit and transliteration. With a live key, open /v1/books/ramayana or /v1/books/mahabharata and append /chapters/1 for the first chapter. For format "prose", show the source citation and render each sections entry’s title and paragraphs. The chapter comes in one response.
book-reader.inputs: GET /v1/books returns up to 24 books. Follow nextCursor as cursor. Fetch /v1/books/{id} for the chapters index, then /v1/books/{id}/chapters/{chapter} using its numeric chapter number. Follow data.nextOffset as offset for more verses. Paid chapter pages contain up to 30 verses. Sandbox shows the opening chapter and first three verses of its sample books.
book-reader.usage: A successful book list, book detail, or chapter page each uses one request. The complete example below makes three calls. Reuse cached indexes and pages when appropriate.

astrology-positions.summary: Show the planets at a specific instant.
astrology-positions.render: Render data.planets with each body, its longitude in degrees and its rashi or nakshatra.
astrology-positions.inputs: datetime must be ISO 8601 with seconds and a UTC offset. Optional ayanamsaDegrees overrides the approximate sidereal offset. The default is a linear Lahiri approximation.

astrology-panchang.summary: Show Panchang elements at a specific instant.
astrology-panchang.render: Render data.panchang.tithi, nakshatra, yoga and karana.
astrology-panchang.inputs: datetime must be ISO 8601 with seconds and a UTC offset. Optional ayanamsaDegrees overrides the approximate sidereal offset. The default is a linear Lahiri approximation.

astrology-chart.summary: Build a Lahiri birth chart with optional Dasha periods.
astrology-chart.render: Use data.charts for divisions, ascendant, planets and houses. Show data.vimshottariDasha when requested.
astrology-chart.inputs: Provide birth with an ISO 8601 datetime including an offset and seconds set to 00, latitude/longitude in decimal degrees, and an IANA timezone matching the offset. Optional divisions are 1 and/or 9. If dashaLevels is greater than zero, include referenceDate as YYYY-MM-DD.

astrology-daily-panchang.summary: Build a local daily Panchang calendar.
astrology-daily-panchang.render: Show data.date, sunrise, sunset, tithi, nakshatra, yoga, karanas and rahuKalam.
astrology-daily-panchang.inputs: Provide a local date (YYYY-MM-DD), latitude and longitude in decimal degrees, and an IANA timezone.

astrology-match.summary: Compare two birth profiles in a compatibility view.
astrology-match.render: Show data.score out of data.maxScore, followed by data.factors.
astrology-match.inputs: Provide person1 and person2. Each needs an ISO 8601 datetime with seconds set to 00 and an offset matching the IANA timezone, plus latitude and longitude in decimal degrees.

astrology-chart-image.summary: Show a North, South or East Indian chart in an app.
astrology-chart-image.render: Use data.contentType and data.imageBase64 to render the chart as a data URI.
astrology-chart-image.inputs: Provide birth with an offset-aware ISO datetime (seconds set to 00), decimal latitude/longitude, and an IANA timezone matching the offset. Optionally choose divisions 1 and/or 9 and layout north, south, or east.

astrology-places.summary: Let a user select a birthplace and time zone.
astrology-places.render: Render data.places as suggestions and keep the selected coordinates and time zone.
astrology-places.inputs: Provide a query of 2–100 characters. Optional country is a two-letter uppercase country code. Optional limit is 1–10. Keep the attribution from data.attribution when displaying place data.

astrology-western-chat.summary: Add a Western astrology question form.
astrology-western-chat.render: Display data.result.reply and prompt for birth details when needs_birth_data is true. Example field: data.result.reply.

astrology-western-natal.render: Show chart placements, houses and angles from data.result. Example field: data.result.planets.

astrology-western-natal-insights.summary: Explain the main patterns in a Western birth chart.
astrology-western-natal-insights.render: Use the natal interpretation returned by the operation.

astrology-western-chart-similarity.summary: Compare a birth chart with a ranked set of similar charts.
astrology-western-chart-similarity.render: Display the ranked matches and their scores from data.result. Example field: data.result.matches.

astrology-western-ephemeris.summary: Show planetary motion for selected dates.
astrology-western-ephemeris.render: Display the dates and planetary positions from data.result. Example field: data.result.data.astrology.

astrology-western-astrocartography.summary: Draw planetary lines on a world map.
astrology-western-astrocartography.render: Draw the returned GeoJSON in WGS84 longitude, latitude order. Example field: data.result.lines.

astrology-western-astrocartography-paran.summary: Show planetary crossing zones on a map.
astrology-western-astrocartography-paran.render: Draw returned GeoJSON bands in longitude, latitude order and label the planetary pairs. Example field: data.result.parans.

astrology-western-astrocartography-reloc.summary: Compare a birth chart at a destination city.
astrology-western-astrocartography-reloc.render: Display the relocated chart and relocation summary from data.result.

astrology-western-astrocartography-recom.summary: Rank destinations for a selected focus.
astrology-western-astrocartography-recom.render: Display destination names, ranking and scores from data.result. Example field: data.result.results.

astrology-western-astrocartography-city.summary: Review a single destination in a relocation view.
astrology-western-astrocartography-city.render: Display the city and focus scores from data.result. Example field: data.result.focus_scores.

astrology-western-wedding-electional.render: Display each candidate time and its rationale when the operation is available.

astrology-western-sun-sign.summary: Add a Sun sign profile card.

docs.title: Make your first Mantrilo API request
docs.lede: One REST API for mantras, sacred audio, scripture books and astrology. Start from a guide for what you’re building, or look up any endpoint. Examples show the response format. Some use excerpts or placeholders.

quick.key: Get a key. Every account starts with a sandbox key.
quick.server: Keep it on your server. Set and in your backend’s environment.
quick.request: Make a request. List one mantra, then follow the endpoint reference or a guide for your goal.

goals.title: Start from your goal
goals.copy: Each guide starts with a request you can run, then shows the server code, pagination and quota.
goals.astrology: Astrology has a guide for every capability.

docs.auth: Send your key on every request as <header/>. The API blocks browser cross-origin calls, so call it from your server and pass only the content to your app. Never put a key in a web bundle, mobile app or repository. If a key leaks, regenerate it in the console; the old key stops working within a minute.

env.label: Key environments
env.sandbox: Sample mantras, the sample books’ opening verses, and available astrology operations. Every account has one.
env.liveReads: The full available catalog. Issued with a paid plan.
env.note: Sandbox and live keep separate usage totals. A sandbox request for an item outside the sample returns 403 sandbox_sample_only.

pagination.cursor: List endpoints return nextCursor. Pass it back as cursor to read the next page. It is null on the last page. Set the page size with limit (1–100).
pagination.offset: Chapter pages return nextOffset. Pass it back as offset to read more verses of the same chapter.

errors.copy: Every error has the same shape. The code is stable; the message explains what to fix. Only successful responses count toward your plan.
errors.label: API errors

rows.invalid_limit: Fix the query parameter named in the message.
rows.invalid_operation: Fix the astrology input named in the message.
rows.invalid_api_key: The key is missing, wrong, or revoked.
rows.plan_inactive: Live keys need an active paid plan.
rows.sandbox_sample_only: That item is outside the sandbox sample. Use your live key.
rows.not_found: No such item, or it has no recording.
rows.method_not_allowed: Use the method listed for the endpoint.
rows.rate_limited: Wait for the Retry-After header, then retry.
rows.quota_exceeded: The monthly allowance has run out.
rows.too_many_failed_attempts: Too many bad keys from one address. Retry later.
rows.internal_error: Retry, and quote the requestId if it continues.
rows.books_unavailable: The service or operation is temporarily unavailable. Retry later.
rows.astrology_timeout: The calculation took too long. Retry. Nothing is charged.

limits.copy: Allowances apply to your whole workspace, not to each key, and reset monthly in UTC. Each successful content response or astrology calculation is one request. Each audio link also counts the file’s size.
limits.label: Plan limits
limits.headers: Responses include X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-Quota-Requests-Remaining and X-Request-Id. A rate_limited response adds Retry-After. Sandbox keys always use the Free rate. If your workspace has no monthly request cap, X-Quota-Requests-Remaining is unlimited.

epics.format: Books return format: "prose" and language: "en". For a chapter, display data.source and iterate over data.sections. Render each section’s title and paragraphs in order. Prose chapters return an empty verses array and nextOffset: null.

accuracy.a: Planetary positions come from an astronomical ephemeris for the exact minute and place you enter. Signs are only uncertain when a body sits right on a sign boundary or the birth time is approximate, so a time to the nearest few minutes gives the best result.

privacy.q: Do you store my birth details?
privacy.a: No. Your date, time and place are sent once to calculate the result and are not saved or logged. The result stays in this browser tab.

zodiac-signs.heading: Find all your signs, Western and Vedic.
zodiac-signs.lede: Enter your birth date, time and place to see your Sun, Moon and Rising signs, and your Vedic Rashi, Lagna, Sun sign and Nakshatra side by side.

about.heading: Why you have two sets of signs
about.p0: Western astrology uses the tropical zodiac, which starts at the March equinox. Vedic (Jyotish) astrology uses the sidereal zodiac, which is fixed to the stars. The two have drifted about 24 degrees apart, so most people’s Vedic signs fall one sign earlier than their Western ones.
about.p1: Your Sun sign depends only on your birth date. Your Moon sign changes every two to three days, and your Rising sign (Lagna in Vedic astrology) changes about every two hours, so those need your birth time and place.

faqs.q0: Why is my Vedic sign different from my Western sign?
faqs.a0: The Vedic zodiac is measured against the fixed stars and the Western zodiac against the seasons. The difference between them, called the ayanamsa, is about 24 degrees today, so a planet at 10° Gemini in the Western zodiac sits at about 16° Taurus in the Vedic one.
faqs.a1: Western astrology leads with the Sun sign. Vedic astrology leads with the Moon sign (Rashi) and the ascendant (Lagna), and uses the Moon’s Nakshatra for names, matching and the Vimshottari Dasha.

sun-sign.heading: What is my Sun sign?
sun-sign.lede: Your Sun sign is the zodiac sign the Sun was in when you were born. Enter your birth date to see it to the degree, along with your Vedic Sun sign.

about.heading: Born on the cusp?
about.p0: The Sun changes sign around the 20th of each month, but the exact moment moves by up to a day from year to year. If you were born near a change, the date alone can’t settle it: add your birth time and place for the exact answer.
about.p1: In Vedic astrology the Sun is measured against the stars, so it enters each sign about three weeks later. That’s why many people are, for example, a Western Gemini but a Vedic Taurus.

faqs.q0: Do I need my birth time for my Sun sign?
faqs.a0: Usually not. The Sun moves about one degree a day, so only people born within a day of a sign change need their birth time and place.
faqs.q1: What are the Sun sign dates?
faqs.a1: Roughly: Aries Mar 21–Apr 19, Taurus Apr 20–May 20, Gemini May 21–Jun 20, Cancer Jun 21–Jul 22, Leo Jul 23–Aug 22, Virgo Aug 23–Sep 22, Libra Sep 23–Oct 22, Scorpio Oct 23–Nov 21, Sagittarius Nov 22–Dec 21, Capricorn Dec 22–Jan 19, Aquarius Jan 20–Feb 18, Pisces Feb 19–Mar 20. The exact boundaries shift slightly each year.

moon-sign.heading: What is my Moon sign?
moon-sign.lede: Your Moon sign is the zodiac sign the Moon was in at the moment you were born. Enter your birth details to find it in both the Western and Vedic zodiacs.

about.heading: Why the Moon needs a birth time
about.p0: The Moon moves about 13 degrees a day and changes sign every two to three days. If it changed sign on your birthday, the time you were born decides which sign it was in.
about.p1: If you don’t know your birth time, leave it blank. The calculator uses midday and tells you when the Moon changed sign that day, so you know whether the answer is certain.

faqs.q0: Is the Moon sign the same as the Rashi?
faqs.a0: In Vedic astrology, yes: your Rashi is your Moon sign in the sidereal zodiac. It is usually one sign earlier than your Western Moon sign.

rising-sign.heading: What is my Rising sign?
rising-sign.lede: Your Rising sign, or ascendant, is the zodiac sign that was rising on the eastern horizon when you were born. Enter your birth date, time and place to find it.

about.heading: Why the exact time matters
about.p0: The whole zodiac rises over the horizon once a day, so the Rising sign changes roughly every two hours, and faster or slower depending on your latitude. Being off by 15 minutes can change it, so use the time on your birth certificate if you can.
about.p1: The place matters too. The calculator uses your birthplace’s coordinates and its historical time zone, including daylight saving time, to work out the exact moment of your birth.

faqs.q0: What if I don’t know my birth time?
faqs.a0: Then your Rising sign can’t be calculated reliably. Your Sun sign and, on most days, your Moon sign still can.
faqs.q1: Is the Rising sign the same as the Lagna?
faqs.a1: They are the same point. The Lagna is the ascendant measured in the Vedic (sidereal) zodiac, so it is usually one sign earlier than the Western Rising sign.

rashi.heading: What is my Rashi?
rashi.lede: Your Rashi is the sign the Moon occupied at your birth in the Vedic (sidereal) zodiac. Enter your birth details to find your Rashi, its lord and your Nakshatra.

about.heading: Rashi in Vedic astrology
about.p0: Vedic astrology gives the Moon sign more weight than the Sun sign. Your Rashi is used for daily horoscopes (rashifal), for Gochar (transits) and, with your Nakshatra, for Kundli matching.
about.p1: This calculator uses the Lahiri (Chitrapaksha) ayanamsa, the standard adopted by the Government of India’s calendar reform committee and used by most Panchangs.

faqs.a0: Mesha (Aries), Vrishabha (Taurus), Mithuna (Gemini), Karka (Cancer), Simha (Leo), Kanya (Virgo), Tula (Libra), Vrishchika (Scorpio), Dhanu (Sagittarius), Makara (Capricorn), Kumbha (Aquarius) and Meena (Pisces).
faqs.q1: Is my Rashi based on my name?
faqs.a1: A name Rashi (naam rashi) is chosen from the first syllable of a name. Your birth Rashi, calculated here, comes from the Moon’s position when you were born and is the one used in a Kundli.

lagna.heading: What is my Lagna?
lagna.lede: Your Lagna is the sign rising on the eastern horizon at your birth, in the Vedic zodiac. It is the first house of your Kundli. Enter your exact birth time and place to find it.

about.heading: The Lagna and your Kundli
about.p0: In a Vedic birth chart the Lagna is the first house, and every other house follows from it. Two people born on the same day in the same city can have different Lagnas only a couple of hours apart.
about.p1: Because the Lagna changes about every two hours, an exact birth time matters. Lagna is calculated here with the Lahiri ayanamsa and whole-sign houses.

faqs.q0: What is the difference between Lagna and Rashi?
faqs.a0: The Lagna is the rising sign at your birth and changes every couple of hours. The Rashi is the Moon’s sign and changes every two to three days. Both come from the same moment.

nakshatra.heading: What is my Nakshatra?
nakshatra.lede: Your birth Nakshatra, or birth star, is the lunar mansion the Moon was in when you were born. Enter your birth details to find it, with its pada and ruling planet.

about.heading: The 27 Nakshatras
about.p0: The Vedic zodiac is divided into 27 Nakshatras of 13°20′ each, and each Nakshatra into four padas (quarters). The Moon passes through about one Nakshatra a day, so the birth time often decides which one is yours.
about.p1: Your Nakshatra’s lord sets the order of your Vimshottari Dasha periods, and its pada gives the traditional first syllable for a name. It is also central to Kundli matching.

faqs.q0: Can I find my Nakshatra without a birth time?
faqs.a0: Only sometimes. The Moon spends about a day in each Nakshatra, so without a time the result may be one of two. The calculator uses midday and you should treat the result as a likely answer.
faqs.a1: Each Nakshatra is split into four padas of 3°20′. The pada narrows down your Moon’s position and links it to a Navamsa (D9) sign.

mantra-api.title: Sanskrit Mantra and Shloka API
mantra-api.intro: Add mantras to your app or website with one REST API. Records bring original Sanskrit together with transliteration and source references where available.
mantra-api.status: Create a free sandbox key to try sample mantras. Fields can be empty on individual records, so check the titles, languages and source details your app needs.

s0.title: Build a reading experience around the verse
s0.copy: A developer can present original text first, offer transliteration alongside it, and add a translation they have permission to distribute. Keep source context close to the text so readers can distinguish a verse from its explanation.

s1.title: Treat optional fields as optional
s1.copy: Mantra verses return Sanskrit and transliteration where available. Translation is null and wordMeanings is empty. Hide missing fields in your app.

s2.title: Keep text and recordings connected
s2.copy: A mantra with a recording includes an audio link in its response. Request the signed recording link through your server, and show a listening control only when that link is present.

s3.title: Confirm provenance before commercial use
s3.copy: A verse’s text, translation, and recording can each carry different rights. Ask for the source and translator details of the records you plan to use, and review the content license status before distribution.

workflow.w0: Receive a selected text record through your server.
workflow.w1: Render original text and available transliteration.
workflow.w2: Show a source reference and linked recording only when supplied.

sacred-audio-api.title: Mantra Recording API
sacred-audio-api.intro: Add sacred audio to devotional apps, learning products, and websites. Mantrilo links recordings to their mantras, so listening stays connected to the words.
sacred-audio-api.status: Recordings are delivered through signed links that last 15 minutes. They are available for mantras where a recording exists.
sacred-audio-api.exampleTitle: A mantra with its recording link

s0.title: A recording belongs with its content
s0.copy: A mantra with a recording includes an audio link in its response. A reading view can reveal a listening control when that link is present and omit it when it isn’t.

s1.title: Load audio when a visitor asks to listen
s1.copy: Request the signed recording link from your server when someone chooses to listen. Each link counts the file’s size toward your monthly allowance, so avoid requesting links during page load.

s2.title: Plan for monthly data delivery
s2.copy: Audio allowances measure the data delivered, not file storage. The pricing page compares each plan’s monthly allowance. Recording length and how often people listen will affect delivery usage. Ask us about recording coverage and formats.

s3.title: Confirm recording-specific permissions
s3.copy: Commercial use is subject to the documented content license. Confirm which recordings are available, how they may be distributed, and what source or performer information can be shown. The software license does not establish recording rights.

workflow.w0: Check whether the displayed content has a recording.
workflow.w1: Request a signed link through your server.
workflow.w2: Start playback after user input and monitor delivered data.

books-api.title: Books API
books-api.intro: Add Hindu scriptures and English retellings of the Ramayana and Mahabharata to your app. Browse books by collection and read chapters with source references.
books-api.status: Browse the catalog by collection. The sandbox shows sample titles and opening verses; a live key can access the full available catalog.

s0.title: Give readers a path through a text
s0.copy: A scripture reader can start at a book overview, move into a chapter, and show individual verses within that chapter. Preserve the book and chapter relationship when linking to a selected passage.

s1.title: Ramayana and Mahabharata retellings
s1.copy: A live key can read all 22 Ramayana chapters and 62 Mahabharata chapters. Each chapter returns a source reference and ordered prose sections with paragraphs.

s2.title: Handle missing translations and references
s2.copy: A reading view should render available original text and display translation or commentary only when supplied. Any verse field can be null, so build the view to leave it out.

s3.title: Review coverage and licensing by title
s3.copy: Start with the Bhagavad Gita and Isha Upanishad in the sandbox. Browse the Library for previews and check the content license before publishing material in an app.
